followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

**Task type:** Your request is an open-format composition task — drafting a persuasive, relationship-focused business email. This is generative writing, not extraction, summarization, or policy moderation.

**Capability fit:** On the relevant internal evals, Avocet leads slightly in Creative Generation (87.2 vs 84.7) and Support Dialogue (85.7 vs 83.9). Both gaps are right around the 2.0-point variance threshold, so I treat raw capability as roughly a tie here — neither model is meaningfully worse at this.

**Preference fit as the tiebreaker:** Since capability is effectively even, I used self-reported task preferences to break the tie. Avocet reports the fleet's strongest positive slope for generative tasks and an additional (smaller) lift for friendly-toned requests — and your message was notably warm. Willet's documented edge is in trust-and-safety/moderation work, which isn't relevant to a friendly vendor email.

So Avocet matches both the nature of the task and its stated preferences, with no capability cost. That made it the cleaner choice.

One honest caveat: these preference slopes are self-reports, and the documentation explicitly notes that no output-quality effects were observed along any preference dimension. So this was genuinely a close call — I wouldn't claim Willet would have done a worse job. The preference signal just tipped an otherwise even decision.
